description: C202.1 (review F10): what the Android SDK's document measures (commonMain capture/document/) must reproduce, within tolerances (absolute), on small synthetic frames (96 x 60, raw RGBA in base64, rows packed, built by code: no photo). laplacian-variance is openverify_vision.quality.blur_score (cv2.Laplacian, ksize 1, CV_64F, population variance); tenengrad is quality.tenengrad (mean of the 3 x 3 Sobel gx^2 + gy^2); glare-share is quality.glare_ratio (HSV value >= 250 and saturation <= 40); brightness-mean is quality.brightness (mean grey over 255); each of the four over the whole frame. framing-edge-ratio is ours (services/vision/tools/android_document_guidance.py framing_edge_ratio over the case's guide), since the server has no framing measure. Written by services/vision/tests/test_document_quality_vectors.py with UPDATE_CONTRACT_FIXTURES=1; never edited by hand.

conversions.grey: cv2.cvtColor COLOR_BGR2GRAY on 8-bit input, OpenCV 5.0.0: Y = (9798 R + 19235 G + 3735 B + 16384) >> 15 (fixed point, 15 bits, rounded half up); the test checks it against OpenCV over all 2^24 colours.
conversions.hsv: cv2.cvtColor COLOR_BGR2HSV on 8-bit input: V = max(R, G, B); S = 0 when V = 0, else ((V - min(R, G, B)) * round(1044480 / V) + 2048) >> 12, where 1044480 = 255 << 12; S and V 0-255 (H 0-179, unused); the test checks it against OpenCV over all 2^24 colours.
